feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Co-presence of Multiple P. copri Complex Clades
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota composition measured as prevalence of P. copri clades in stool samples from Westernized and non-Westernized populations.

value: 1,023 high-quality P. copri genomes reconstructed from 6,874 metagenomes
Four genetically distinct P. copri clades (A, B, C, D) with inter-clade divergence >10%
P. copri genomes from 22 different countries across 6 continents
61.6% of non-Westernized individuals carried all four P. copri clades
4.6% of Westernized individuals carried all four clades
Ancient DNA from 5,300-year-old Iceman and pre-Columbian coprolites contained P. copri
P. copri clade divergence estimated at ~6.5 million years ago
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 1,023 high-quality P. copri genomes reconstructed from 6,874 metagenomes spanning 6 continents and 22 countries
uncurated_metadata.section: Results — Analysis of >1,000 P. copri Genomes Reveals Four Clades
uncurated_metadata.notes: Key findings from metagenomic analysis and population structure study of P. copri.

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a common human gut microbe; human intestinal microbiome
host_species.notes: P. copri is explicitly described as a human gut microbe; all samples are from human participants (Ethiopian, Ghanaian, Tanzanian cohorts, and ancient human remains).
